thread:
anne_dev: Rolling back rollout — apac-a10 pool p95 jumped from 120ms -> 420ms after merge abc1234. Rollout blocked. Details: KV cache hit rate falling, more kernel fallbacks observed. @sasha_perf can you share perf traces? :eyes:

sasha_perf: Looking. I pulled a perf sample from a live request on one of the affected nodes. Early sign: kernel selector fell back to generic GEMM path under moderate packet loss. Snip from logs:
```
kernel_selector: preferred=opt_matmul_v2, fallback=generic_matmul, reason=rt-net-loss
selected_kernel=generic_matmul seq=512 hw=A10
```
KV hit rate for that node: 18% -> 6% during spike.

mike_runtime: That pattern sounds like repeated retransmits increasing tail latency and changing sequence length distribution, which trips a heuristic to prefer safer kernels. Can we confirm packet stats? @kevin_sre

kevin_sre: Checked NIC counters on a node in asia-southeast2-apac-a10-1. Showed a burst of retransmits and RSC drops around the same time window. `ethtool -S eth0` excerpt:
```
rx_errors: 0
rx_dropped: 12
tx_retransmit: 144
rsc_aggregation_drops: 7
```
Also saw offload kickouts after a firmware patch.

julia: CI caught a perf regression on the merge too: perf-run/latency-smoke failed on the merge pipeline with p95 regression in a10-shard tests. CI link: https://ci.internal/12345 :grimacing:

ci-bot: perf-run/latency-smoke (#4512) — FAILURE — p95 increased 3.1x compared to baseline. Artifact: perf-sample-1812345.tar.gz

mike_runtime: Proposed bisect: isolate between commit abc1234 (good) and def5678 (bad). Quick bisect script:
```
git bisect start
git bisect bad def5678
git bisect good abc1234
# run perf smoke job
```
If kernel selector heuristic is influenced by network metrics, we should also reproduce with `tc qdisc netem loss 0.5%` to validate.

sasha_perf: I ran a controlled repro in staging with `tc` and saw the selector flip rule when measured RTT jitter exceeded 8ms and packet loss >0.3%. KV cache eviction rate spiked because many requests got slight truncation in prefix matches. Patch X removed a guard that kept the old selector from observing packet-level signals.

anne_dev: So candidate root cause: merge def5678 introduced change to selector that reads ephemeral net stats and penalizes optimized kernels, combined with recent NIC firmware changes causing transient packet loss — leads to KV churn and tail latency. Rollout remains blocked. :no_good:

julia: I'm preparing a revert PR for def5678 to hold the release. Can someone run a quick canary revert in staging and report p95?

sasha_perf: Canary revert applied on staging. Results: p95 back to 130ms, KV hit rate restored to ~20%. No network anomaly during the canary window.

deploy-bot: Rollout to apac-a10 paused by anne_dev at 1812345690. :lock:

anne_dev: Good work. Next steps: revert in production, coordinate with SRE to roll NIC firmware audit, add a guard in kernel selector to ignore short-lived net spikes, and add perf CI test that injects small packet loss. I'll open followups.

mike_runtime: I'll own the selector guard change and the CI injection. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
